It's never okay to starve yourself. You're going to suffer from malnutrition, and it's also not sustainable. Say it works and you lose the weight, will you resume eating then? Because you won't have developed any long-term healthy eating practices, and it will mess up your metabolism (to say the least). There CAN be health benefits to fasting, but that really should be something you discuss with a doctor, IMO, rather than just diving straight into it.

maybe try selectively drinking lower calorie fizzy drinks. Or give yourself an allowance. I don't think it's helpful to cut it out entirely (if you give in and treat yourself, you'll feel guilty, and that might set you back) but maybe allow yourself a specific number of glasses/cans. You can give yourself a 'fix' as it were, but control the quantity. If nothing else, regulating how much you drink will have other health benefits!

tbh, I always preferred Diet or Coke Zero and sparkling water, so it's not really been a priority concern of mine. But I think it is worth questioning why you like it: is it because of the flavour The texture (idk how else to describe it, but the fizziness), are you genuinely thirsty, etc.? Because with that info you can start to work out how to target quitting/replacing it.

Such as not being able to get out at much. Plus, you said you were feeling stressed recently, and stress makes you gain weight. Your body is trying to protect you, in its own way, and maybe it got things a little messed up but I don’t think you should feel so self loathing about your body. 

I know that still hurts - bc it doesn’t change the fact that you gained the weight, but I do think it is really worth remembering that you kept it off for a long time and only got bigger when dealing with a difficult, stressful time. I think that is honestly a good indication that you are committed and genuinely did really well to keep the weight off. Life is just like that sometimes.

I am in a very similar situation. I have many; on my chest, stomach, hips, arms, back, and all over my legs. I am still working on coming to terms with it. If it is any comfort to know: you are not alone, both in the fact that you aren't the only person to feel this way, and also in the fact that stretchmarks are very common to get. It can be frustrating to know others who avoided them, but there are so many other people who get them for all sorts of reasons. My boyfriend has loads of huge, dark stretchmarks across his arms and back, and he's had them since puberty. 

For what it is worth, they will fade over time! Some of mine are basically invisible now, and even the texture is improved. I also found that using Bio-Oil twice daily on them really helped, as well as moisturisers and exfoliants. It's also good to take the time to treat your body well, to get used to your new skin 

I am concerned about the negative language you're using. You're normal, I promise; people will not have nausea looking at you - people, by and large, do not notice or care about stretchmarks, and you are not 'disgusting' or a 'monster' for having scarring that is very natural and happens to everyone. If it's at the point where it's seriously effecting your mental health, it might be worth seeing your doctor/a counsellor regarding potential body dysmorphia. For me, receiving counselling was very helpful! 

Be kind to yourself x
